Sha256Hex.description: Owning decoder enforces the same exact digest shape as the JSON schema.

Frame.description:
The effective frame: fully resolved before evaluation (spec §27.1).

A context handle pins this frame (plus expiry/owner in the service
layer). The frame never stores a hidden current-world selection: world
focus is per supporting request (spec §11.3, §27.1, I24).

context.description:
The represented context record (objective reality, a character's
beliefs, a source narrative, ...).

readerScene.description: Exact authored scene defining reader disclosure order.

personalSequence.description:
Optional personal experienced sequence (spec §7.1): a separately
declared ordering, never inferred.

UniverseId.description: Stable identity of a named universe (top-level storage and reference boundary).

ContinuityId.description: Stable identity of a continuity (one canon revision head).

RevisionId.description: Stable identity of an immutable canon revision.

RecordRef.description:
A canonical record reference with an explicit universe namespace
(spec §27.1). The namespace may be omitted in *wire* input where the
required `universe` argument supplies it; the service expands and rejects
conflicting namespaces before storage. Canonical payloads always carry it.

universe.description: Universe namespace. `None` only in wire input pending expansion.

record.description:
Stable record identity (resolved through the requested revision's
membership map — spec §27.1).

RecordId.description: Stable identity of a canonical record within a universe.

FrameTime.description: The temporal part of a frame.

oneOf.description:
All validities: the query makes no temporal claim (spec §27.1:
"an explicitly timeless/all-validities query").
Evaluate at or within this temporal expression.

State at the moment of a specific event (entry/exit framing
is handled by the event's own time; this names the anchor).

TemporalExpression.description:
The temporal value type (spec §5.3, §7.1).

Intervals are half-open `[start, end)` where exact interval algebra
applies (spec §7.1); the author-facing display must explain boundary
meaning (S26).

oneOf.description: Exact instant in a named calendar.

Interval. Where both endpoints are exact, semantics are half-open
`[start, end)`.

Approximate moment ("about ten days in" is not an exact ten-day
duration without an author definition — spec §5.3).
A duration in the calendar's own unit structure.
Relative ordering constraint against another record's time.
No temporal claim: the author did not define one.

CalendarId.description: Stable identity of a calendar / temporal reference system definition.

TemporalBound.description:
How a boundary of an interval is known (spec §27.2).

`Unknown` and `Unbounded` are deliberately distinct (S27): an undefined
endpoint is not silently infinite or zero-length.

oneOf.description: No bound: the interval extends without limit in that direction.
The author has not established the endpoint.
Exact point, as a string in the named calendar's unit structure.
Approximate point with declared uncertainty.

uncertainty.description:
Boxed: `Value` may embed `TemporalExpression`, so one side of
the mutual recursion must be indirect (infinite-size rule).

oneOf.description: Bounded but not exact: the endpoint lies within this range of points.
Preserves the author's exact Unicode string content (spec §27.8).
Exact integers are decimal digit strings, never host floats.
Exact decimal quantities, preserved at authored precision.

`Quantity(value, unit_id)`. Conversion requires an explicit
compatible unit definition (spec §5.3).

Struct variants (not newtype) for the reference/expression forms:
serde's internally-tagged newtype form would inline the content's
fields into the tagged map (duplicate `kind` key when the content is
itself tagged) and hit the recursion limit for recursive content.
Field keys match the canonical impl below.
Ordered; authored sequence order is canonical (spec §27.2).
Set semantics: normalized by stable identity at the service.

UnitId.description: Stable identity of a unit definition record.

SpatialExpression.description:
A qualitative spatial expression (spec §7.4).

Ownership, custody, containment, control, occupancy, legal access,
physical access, and knowledge of an entrance are separate predicates:
only the qualitative relations below live in values; the predicates
themselves are definitions.

ValueDefinitionId.description: Stable identity of a structured value definition record.

TemporalRelation.description: A relation between two times without inventing dates (spec §7.1).

oneOf.description: Strict before. Cycles within one declared acyclic ordering are invalid (S28).
Strict after.
Starts and ends within.
Time ranges overlap (may be definite, indeterminate, or refuted).
Same instant (exact only).

EventTimeSide.description:
Which side of an event a frame observes (spec §30.2 event entry/exit
selector). Preconditions see `Before`; effects see `After`.

oneOf.description: The pre-event state.
The post-event state.

Perspective.description:
How a query views the universe (spec §8.3).

Author-known truth, character perspective, and reader disclosure are
separate views. Author permissions are a security dimension; a
point-of-view filter is not an access-control mechanism unless the
author explicitly configures a restricted principal.

oneOf.description: The author's omniscient view of the universe.
A character's fictional knowledge (bounded by records).
A source/narrator's depicted view.
Reader disclosure position.

PrincipalId.description: Stable identity of an authenticated application principal.

AssessmentVersionRef.description: Exact workflow evidence references use the existing domain wire keys and IDs.

RecordVersionId.description: Stable identity of an immutable record version.

Polarity.description: Support or refutation of a proposition (spec §5.2).
